question: Name two optional pavement-marking features explicitly labeled in Figure 3D-1 at the roundabout.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 3D-1 explicitly labels several optional pavement-marking features at the roundabout. Two of these are (1) the optional white diagonal markings on the approach adjacent to the splitter island, and (2) the yellow edge line around the inner (left-hand) edge of the circulatory roadway, which is labeled "Optional" in the figure. (The YIELD word marking on approaches is likewise an optional feature shown in the figure.) Options (permitted): - "A yellow edge line may be placed around the inner (left-hand) edge of the circulatory roadway (see Figure 3D-1) and may be used to channelize traffic." - "YIELD (word) (see Figure 3D-1) and YIELD AHEAD (symbol or word) pavement markings may be used on approaches to roundabouts." Guidance (recommended): - Where a white edge line is used for the circulatory roadway, it should be "A. A solid line adjacent to the splitter island, and B. A wide dotted line across the lane(s) entering the roundabout" (see Figure 3D-1) — context for the labeled edge-line treatments in the figure. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 3D-1 shows a callout reading "Optional white diagonal markings" pointing to the hatched white markings on the east approach, and an "Optional" callout pointing to the yellow line around the inner edge of the circulatory roadway; another "Optional" callout points to the YIELD word marking on the south entry. [Image 2] is the full page 596 view of Figure 3D-1 confirming the same labeled features, including the "Optional" labels and "Optional white diagonal markings" callout. Citations: - Section 3D.03 Option §4 (p.605) - Section 3D.05 Option §1 (p.605) - Section 3D.03 Guidance §2 (p.595) - Figure 3D-1 (p.596)
gold_answer: Optional diagonal markings in the splitter island and an optional wide dotted extension of the circulatory roadway edge line.
